Title: Select/ Edit Pattern Symbols
Content: Objective Select or delete Pattern Symbols. Location Main Menu 2D Pattern Pattern Annotation Pattern Symbol/ Edit Annotation 2D Toolbar Pattern Annotation/ Edit Annotation Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu 2D Pattern Pattern Annotation Pattern Symbol/ Edit Annotation 2D Toolbar Pattern Annotation/ Edit Annotation Click the Pattern outline or Internal Line where a Pattern Symbol is added. The Pattern Symbol is selected and highlighted in yellow. Hit the Delete key on the keyboard or right click on the Pattern Symbol and select the Delete option. The selected Pattern Symbol is deleted. Note: To select all Pattern Symbols, please hit the Ctrl+A keys on the keyboard at once.

Title: Select/Move Pattern Annotation
Content: List of Contents Select/Move Pattern Annotation Moving Pattern Annotation Deleting Pattern Annotation Select/Move Pattern Annotation - Create and edit Pattern Annotation on Patterns in the 2D Window. - Select the Pattern Annotation tool from the 2D toolbar. Moving Pattern Annotation - Select the Select/Move Pattern Annotation tool from the 2D toolbar. - Navigate to the 2D Window. - Click and drag the pattern annotation to be moved. Deleting Pattern Annotation - With the Select/Move Pattern Annotation tool selected, right click on the pattern annotation to be deleted. - Click DELETE. The selected pattern annotation will be deleted. - Or, select the pattern annotation and hit Delete key on the keyboard.

Title: Add Dart with Fullness (ver 5.2)
Content: Objective Add fullness to a Pattern while adding a Dart. Location Main Menu 2D Pattern Edit Edit Pattern 2D Toolbar Edit Pattern Operation Select the tool/menu indicated in Location. Right-click on the point where the Dart needs to be created and select Add Dart with Fullness. A reference line extended from the selected point to the mouse cursor appears. Click on a Pattern outline. The Pattern is divided in half based on the reference line. Select a side or the center to add the Dart. Then, move the mouse cursor the adjust the size of the Dart. A preview of the adjusted Pattern with the Dart and fullness appears. Move the mouse cursor along the centerline to assign the length of the Dart. A Dart is added with fullness according to the assigned width and length. Note: Right-click while setting the width and length of the Dart to input specific values.

Title: Clone Pattern with Linked Editing – Instance Pattern
Content: List of Contents Instance Pattern Apply Instance Pattern Instance Pattern - Duplicate Patterns with the linked editing function to edit them identically at the same time. Apply Instance Pattern - Navigate to the 2D toolbar and select the Transform Pattern tool or the Edit Pattern tool. - Right-click on the Pattern to be duplicated and select Clone Pattern with Linked Editing Instance Pattern. - The duplicated Pattern will follow along with the mouse cursor. - Click on the 2D window to paste the duplicated Pattern. - The linked Patterns will be highlighted in yellow-green. - Since the Patterns are linked, they can be edited simultaneously.

Title: Snap to Pattern
Content: Objective Activate Snap to Pattern to create and edit Internal Shapes and Sewing Lines that accurately fit the point and line. Location Main Menu Preferences Snap to Pattern Right-Click Pop-Up Menu (on 2D Window) Snap to Pattern Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Preferences Snap to Pattern Right-Click Pop-Up Menu (on 2D Window) Snap to Pattern Create or edit Internal Shapes and Sewing Lines while Snap to Pattern is activated. The Internal Shapes and Sewing Lines snap to the closest point or line. Note: Snap to Pattern is activated by default. Check off the option to deactivate the function.

Title: Apply Linked Editing – Instance Pattern
Content: List of Contents Instance Pattern Apply Instance Pattern Remove Instance Pattern Instance Pattern - Edit identical Patterns simultaneously. Apply Instance Pattern - Navigate to the 2D toolbar and select the Transform Pattern tool or Edit Pattern tool. - Right-click on the Patterns to be linked and select Apply Linked Editing Instance Pattern from the pop-up menu. - The linked Patterns will be highlighted in yellow-green. - The linked Patterns can be edited at the same time. Remove Instance Pattern - Navigate to the 2D toolbar and select the Transform Pattern tool or the Edit Pattern tool. - Right-click on the Patterns to be unlinked and select Remove Linked Editing from the pop-up menu. - The linked Patterns will be separated. - The Patterns can be edited individually.

Title: Pattern Symbol
Content: List of Contents Pattern Symbol Create Pattern Symbol - Add or delete guidelines for garment construction. - Main Menu 2D Pattern Pattern Annotation Pattern Symbol - 2D Toolbar Pattern Symbol Create Create a Single Pattern Symbol - Click the Pattern outline or Internal Line where a Pattern Symbol should be added. - A Pattern Symbol is added to the selected segment. - Place on Fold symbol is added by default. Create Multiple Pattern Symbols - To create Pattern Symbols on multiple segments, hold down the Shift key while selecting desired segments. - Or, click and drag or use lasso selection to apply Pattern symbols to multiple segments.

Title: Edit Pattern Instruction Lines
Content: List of Contents Pattern Instruction Line Properties Edit Properties Pattern Instruction Line Properties - Edit properties for Pattern Symbols as needed. - Navigate to the Main Menu and select 2D Pattern Pattern Annotation Pattern Symbol or Edit Annotation. - Select the Edit Annotation or Pattern Symbol tool from the 2D toolbar. Edit Properties - Select the Pattern Symbol to be modified. - Navigate to the Property Editor to view the selected Pattern Symbols properties. Name - Rename the Pattern Symbol. Line Type - Select the type of the Pattern Symbol as needed. Flip - This option only appears when the Pattern Symbol is created on an Internal Line. - Toggle on the option to place the Pattern Symbol on the other side of the Internal Line.

Title: Apply Linked Editing – Symmetry Pattern
Content: List of Contents Symmetry Pattern Apply Symmetry Pattern Remove Symmetry Pattern Symmetry Pattern - Edit identical Patterns symmetrically at the same time. Apply Symmetry Pattern - Navigate to the 2D toolbar and select the Transform Pattern tool or Edit Pattern tool. - Right-click on the Patterns to be linked and select Apply Linked Editing Symmetry Pattern from the pop-up menu. - The symmetrized Patterns will be highlighted in light blue. - The symmetrized Patterns can be edited symmetrically at the same time. Remove Symmetry Pattern - Navigate to the 2D toolbar and select the Transform pattern tool or Edit Pattern tool. - Right-click on the Patterns to be unlinked and select Remove Linked Editing from the pop-up menu. - The symmetrized Patterns will be separated. - The Patterns can be edited individually.

Title: Deactivate (Pattern Only)/Activate
Content: Objective Deactivated Patterns are considered as nonexistence in the 3D window. Therefore the rest of the Patterns simulate through the deactivated Patterns. The function is generally used to keep complicated details such as pleats or slits, from avoiding collapsing. When deactivating certain Patterns, the Simulation speed gets faster as it excludes them from calculation. Location 3D Toolbar Select/Move 3D Garment Right-Click Pop-up Menu Deactivate (Pattern Only) / Activate 2D Toolbar Transform Pattern 2D Pattern Right-Click Pop-up Menu Deactivate (Pattern Only) / Activate Operation Follow the indicated guideline: 3D Toolbar Select/Move 3D Garment Right-Click Pop-up Menu Deactivate (Pattern Only) / Activate 2D Toolbar Transform Pattern 2D Pattern Right-Click Pop-up Menu Deactivate (Pattern Only) / Activate The selected Pattern is now being deactivated/activated.

Title: Smart Arrangement
Content: Smart Arrangement - Arrange the Patterns near their sewn pairs maintaining their drape. - Choose the Select/Move tool from the 3D toolbar and navigate to the 3D window. - Right-click on the 3D Garment and select Smart Arrangement. - The selected Pattern will be arranged next to the sewn pair without distortion of the drape.

Title: Graphic (3D Pattern)
Content: List of Contents Graphic 3D Pattern Add Graphic Graphic3D Pattern - Add Graphics to 3D Garments in the 3D window. - Select the Graphic (3D Pattern) tool from the 3D toolbar. - Or, navigate to the Main Menu and select Material Graphic Graphic(3D Pattern) Add Graphic - When the Graphic(3D Pattern) tool is selected, the File Browser will appear. - Select the image file to be added. The mouse cursor will change to the graphic icon. - Click on the position where the graphic should be added. - The Add Graphic window will appear. - Enter values to Width and Height, and click OK. - The graphic will be added based on the settings.

Title: Deactivate (Pattern Only)
Content: List of Contents Deactivate (Pattern Only) Result of Deactivate (Pattern Only) Features of Deactivate (Pattern Only) Deactivate (Pattern Only) - Deactivate selected Patterns to easily perform meticulous editing on the 3D Garment. - Select desired Patterns to be deactivated and right click to access the pop-up menu. Then, select Deactivate (Pattern Only). Result of Deactivate (Pattern Only) - When the selected Patterns are properly deactivated, Patterns should turn translucent navy. When the Simulation is activated, deactivated Patterns will not move, but sewing lines will still be activated. - To activate the selected Patterns, right click again and select Activate. Features of Deactivate (Pattern Only) - Deactivated Patterns will not be calculated for collision. - Simulate overlapped Patterns, one being activated and the other being deactivated. The activated Pattern will easily pass through the deactivated Pattern.

Title: Create Pattern Symbols
Content: Objective Add pattern instruction markings on 2D Patterns using with Pattern Symbols. Location Main Menu 2D Pattern Pattern Annotation Pattern Symbol 2D Toolbar Pattern Symbol Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu 2D Pattern Pattern Annotation Pattern Symbol 2D Toolbar Pattern Symbol Hover the mouse over the Pattern outline or Internal Line where Pattern Symbol is to be added. The Pattern outline or Internal Line is highlighted in light-blue. Click on the segment. A Pattern Symbol is created on the selected segment. The Place on Fold 1 mark is added by default. Note: To create a Pattern Symbol on multiple segments, please select all Pattern outlines or Internal Lines while holding down the Shift key on the keyboard. Or, click and drag on the 2D window, or use the Polygon Lasso Selection function to select multiple segments at once. To hide or show Pattern Symbols, right click on the 2D window with the Edit Pattern tool and select Show Annotations. (Below ver4.0) Main Menu Display 2D Information Show Annotations (ver5.0 or later) 2D Window 2D Information Display Show Annotations (ver5.0 or later)

Title: Apply Linked Editing – Symmetry Pattern (with Sewing)

Title: Graphic (2D Pattern)
Content: List of Contents Graphic (2D Pattern) Add Graphic Graphic (2D Pattern) - Add Graphics to Patterns in the 2D window. - Select the Graphic(2D Pattern) tool from the 2D toolbar. - Or, navigate to the Main Menu and select Materials Graphic Graphic(2D Pattern). Add Graphic - When the Graphic(2D Pattern) tool is selected, the File Browser will appear. - Select the image file to be added. Content: List of Contents Pattern Symbol Select Delete Pattern Symbol - Select or delete selected Pattern Symbol. - Main Menu 2D Pattern Pattern Annotation Pattern Symbol or Edit Annotation. - 2D Toolbar Pattern Symbol or Edit Annotation. Title: Edit Pattern Symbol Properties
Content: Objective Edit Pattern Symbol's properties to meet your needs. Location Main Menu 2D Pattern Pattern Annotation Pattern Symbol/ Edit Annotation 2D Toolbar Pattern Symbol/ Edit Annotation Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu 2D Pattern Pattern Annotation Pattern Symbol/ Edit Annotation 2D Toolbar Pattern Symbol/ Edit Annotation Click on the Pattern Symbol to be edited. The selected Pattern Symbol's properties appear in the Property Editor. Refer to the below table and configure each option as needed. Option Description Name Change the name of the selected Pattern Symbol Line Type Select the desired line type for the Pattern Symbol Place on Fold 1 Place on Fold 2 Directional Line 1 Directional Line 2 Stretch Shrink Gather Cut Line Flip When the Flip option is toggled On, the Pattern Symbol is reflected to the other side based on the Internal Line.

Title: Smart Arrangement
Content: Objective Arrange a new Pattern onto an existing Pattern while maintaining 3D draping state (ver3.0.0). Location 3D Toolbar Select/Move 3D Pattern Right-Click Pop-Up Menu Smart Arrangement Operation Utilizing the 2D sewing tools, sew a new Pattern to an existing Pattern that is being draped. Follow the indicated guideline below: 3D Toolbar Select/Move 3D Pattern Right-Click Pop-Up Menu Smart Arrangement The selected Pattern is now being arranged to where it is sewn as draped.

Title: Select/Move/Transform Pattern
Content: List of Contents Select Move Transform/ Rotate Objective Select Patterns to move, transform and rotate. Location Main Menu 2D Pattern Edit Transform Pattern 2D Toolbar Transform Pattern Operation Select Select the tool indicated. Click a pattern or hold down the Shift key to multi-select patterns. The corresponding pattern is selected. Or, click and drag on the 2D window to encompass all Patterns to be selected with a marquee box. All Patterns inside the marquee box are selected. Note: Right-click on the pattern Select All Sewn(Ctrl+Alt+A) menu, the pattern and the sewn pattern are automatically selected (ver 7.3) Move Select the tool indicated. Click and drag the Pattern to be moved or use the arrow keys on keyboard. Hold down the Shift key or Ctrl key (Mac: command) while moving the Pattern. The Pattern can be moved in precise vertical, horizontal, or diagonal lines, or in its slope. Or, right click or hit F1 key (Mac: Ctrl) while moving the Pattern to type in distance moved. Transform/ Rotate Select the tool indicated. Select the Pattern. The pivot and scale guide appear. Double click the pivot point to activate and transform or rotate based on the pivot point, Click and drag a point or rotation point on the scale guide. The Pattern is transformed and rotated based on the activated pivot. Note: To select point or segment, use the Transform Point/Segment tool.

Content: List of Contents Symmetry Pattern Apply Symmetry Pattern Symmetry Pattern - Duplicate Patterns symmetrically with the linked editing function to edit Patterns simultaneously. Apply Symmetry Pattern - Navigate to the 2D toolbar and select the Transform Pattern tool or the Edit Pattern tool. - Right-click on the Pattern to be duplicated and select Clone Pattern with Linked Editing Symmetry Pattern. - The duplicated Pattern will follow along with the mouse cursor. - Click on the 2D window to paste the duplicated Pattern. - The symmetrized Patterns will be highlighted in light blue. - Since the Patterns are symmetrized, they can be edited symmetrically at the same time.

Title: Flatten
Content: List of Contents Flatten Extract Pattern Flatten - Extract Patterns based on the shapes on an Avatar, drawn with Line (Avatar.) - Select the Flatten tool from the 3D toolbar. - Or, navigate to the Main Menu 3D Garment Flatten. Extract pattern Extract Pattern - Select desired shapes on the Avatar to extract Patterns. - Hover the mouse over the shapes to the extracted. - The shape is highlighted in light-blue. - Click all shapes to be extracted. - Hit the Enter key on the keyboard. - The selected shapes are extracted as Patterns and appear in both the 3D and 2D windows. - The Default Fabric is automatically applied to Patterns that are extracted using the Flatten tool. - Patterns adjacent to each other are sewn automatically. - The Line (Avatar) remains on the Avatar. Extract Pattern by Selecting All - Press Ctrl+A on the keyboard while the Flatten tool is selected, to extract all Patterns. - All Patterns are selected. - Hit the Enter key on the keyboard. - All selected shapes are extracted as Patterns and appear in both of the 3D and 2D windows. - The Default Fabric is automatically applied to Patterns that are extracted using the Flatten tool. - Patterns adjacent to each other are sewn automatically. - The Line (Avatar) remains on the Avatar. Cancel Selection Cancel Individually - Reselect the shape to cancel selection individually. Cancel All - To cancel all selections, hit the Esc key on the keyboard or Ctrl+Z at the same time.

Title: Offset Pattern Outline
Content: Offset Pattern Outline Offset Pattern Outline - Extend the Pattern outline while maintaining the shape of the Pattern. Offset a Segment - Select the Edit Pattern tool from the 2D toolbar. - Navigate to the 2D window, right click on a segment of a Pattern and select Offset Pattern Outline from the pop-up menu. - The Offset Pattern Outline Window will appear. Distance: set how much the Offset Pattern Outline will be apart from the original Pattern outline. Number of Offsets: set how many offsets will be duplicated. Total Distance: total distance equals to the result of Distance multiplying Number of Offsets. Create Internal Line: toggle on to convert the original Pattern outline as an Internal Line. Extend Side Segments: toggle on the option to extend adjacent Pattern outlines, maintaining their original slope. Default Corner, Right Angled Corner, and Unfilled Corner: decide how corners of the offset Pattern outline will be shaped. This option is not used when offsetting a segment. Offset an Entire Pattern - Select the Transform Pattern tool or the Edit Pattern tool from the 2D toolbar. - Navigate to the 2D window, right click on a Pattern and select Offset Pattern Outline from the pop-up menu. - The Offset Pattern Outline Window will appear. Distance: set how much the Offset Pattern Outline will be apart from the original pattern outline. Number of Offsets: set how many offsets will be duplicated. Total Distance: total distance equals to the result of Distance multiplying Number of Offsets. Create Internal Line: toggle on to convert the original Pattern outline as an Internal Line. Extend Side Segments: toggle on the option to extend adjacent Pattern outlines, maintaining their original slope. This is not used when offsetting an entire Pattern. Default Corner, Right Angled Corner, and Unfilled Corner: decide how corners of the offset Pattern outline will be shaped. The Pattern outline will be offset based on the setting.

Title: Create/Edit Pattern Annotation
Content: List of Contents Create Pattern Annotation Edit Pattern Annotation Objective Add annotation to Patterns where it is needed. Location 2D Toolbar Pattern Annotation Operation Create Pattern Annotation Follow the indicated guideline below: 2D Toolbar Pattern Annotation Click and drag on the Pattern to add the annotation. The annotation field appears on the selected position. Type necessary contents into the field and click Ctrl+Enter key on the keyboard or click on the Pattern. The Pattern annotation is added as it appears in blue on the Pattern. Edit Pattern Annotation Follow the indicated guideline below: 2D Toolbar Pattern Annotation Hover over the previously created Pattern annotation. The mouse cursor changes to the following image. Click on the Pattern annotation. The annotation field is activated again.

Title: Edit 2D POM
Content: List of Contents Move Option Objective Move Point/Segment or delete POM. Watch Tutorial Video here Location Main Menu 2D Pattern Point of Measure Edit Point of Measure 2D Toolbar Edit Point of Measure Operation Move Click on a point or a whole segment of the POM to be edited. The point or segment is selected. A pop-up menu appears when multiple POM points are overlapped. Drag to the desired position. The POM is moved to the position. Similar to creating a POM, the line linking two Patterns is maintained as a link in the case of Group POM. When moving Segment and Curved points of a curved POM, hold down the D key on the keyboard and click-and-drag to move the selected points only. The selected point is moved. Option Right click on POM to set the options as needed. Delete Delete the selected POM. Reverse Reverse the direction of the POM. Segment Type/ Straight Type Apply as Pattern Outline or Straight Line. X/ Y Dist Type Show the X/ Y axis distance based on the selected outline. Note: POM is moved when its intersected Pattern Oulines and Internal Lines are moved.

Title: Walk Pattern
Content: Objective Compare the length of two segments of different Patterns in real-time by temporarily aligning each other. Location Main Menu 2D Pattern Walk Pattern 2D Toolbar Walk Pattern Operation Follow the indicated path below: Main Menu 2D Pattern Walk Pattern 2D Toolbar Walk Pattern Click on a point or a part of a pattern outline. The point or the part of a pattern outline is selected and an arrow appears in between the selected point and the mouse cursor. Click on a point or a part of a pattern outline of the pattern to be compared with the one selected at step 2. The preview of the pattern selected at step 2 moves next to the clicked position. Move the mouse cursor along the pattern outline: The preview moves along the pattern outline. The length of the segment appears at the center of the yellow guideline. Hit enter on the keyboard to complete pattern-walking. Note: During pattern length comparison, right-click to set options for adding notches to Walked/Stationary Pattern, Move Walked Pattern to Intersection and Flip Horizontally (ver 6.1).

Title: 2D Pattern (DXF) Import/Export
Content: List of Contents Import DXF / Import DXF (Add) Export DXF Objective DXF is a standard file format of industrial CAD patterns and stores 2D pattern information. DXF is currently available in Yuka, Gerber, Lectra, StyleCAD, Optitex, PAD System, etc. DXF-AAMA, DXF-ASTM, Standard DXF(ver 6.2) files are compatible with most 2D CAD softwares. Note: The options for exporting DXF files are different for each CAD and the method of organizing the pattern information is different. When importing DXF files on CLO 3D, there may be some problems. In this case, please send the problem file to CONTACT US and we will solve it. Location Main Menu File Import / Import (Add) / Export DXF Operation Import DXF / Import DXF (Add) Select the tool/menu indicated. The file explorer window appears. Select the DXF file and click the Open. Import DXF window appears. Set the details and click OK. Basic Scale Select the unit used in the pattern CAD. Rotation Rotate the entire pattern clockwise/counterclockwise. Option Import Pattern Annotation Import Pattern Annotation information together. Auto-Trace as Internal Line The entire baseline is traced as an Internal Line. Swap Cutting Line and Sewing Line Check this option when the pattern's Cutting lines and Sewing lines are changed. * The Cutting line and Sewing line may change depending on the export option setting of the pattern CAD. Include Notches When changing the Sewing line and Cutting Line, the notch is moved together. Auto Distribute Closely rearrange the patterns in the DXF file. Optimize All Curve Points Optimizes the number of curve points in the DXF file. Convert to Seam Allowance (ver 6.1) Import CAD seam allowance to CLO seam allowance. Note: The default setting is applied to the type of start, end or edge seam allowance that is not supported by CLO. Remove Non-Grading Points (ver 6.1) Optimize the number of points by deleting Straight/Curve Points that have no grading information. Note: This option is only required for AAMA-format DXF files which is different from CLO's default curve points. Note: Standard DXF files of AutoCAD and Adobe Illustrator can be imported (ver 6.2) Export DXF Select the tool/menu indicated in Location. The file explorer window appears. Set the file name and save the path and click OK. The DXF Export window appears. Set the details and click OK. Basic Select Pattern Select the size group you want to export from among the grading size groups applied to the file. Only one Size Group can be selected and exported per file. DXF Format Set the export format. Size format (ver 7.0) Export the grading information by including it in the DXF file or RUL file only. Scale Set the unit of the pattern. Rotation Rotate the entire pattern clockwise/counterclockwise. Option Export without Grading Export the current size only excluding grading information. Export without Baselines Export patterns except for baselines. Duplicate Notch on Seam Allowance Duplicate the notch on the outline of the pattern to the seam allowance. Swap Cutting Line and Sewing Line The type of sewing line and the cutting line defined in CLO and Pattern CAD may be different. In this case, when exporting to DXF, the cutting line and the sewing line are replaced and exported. Convert Curve Point to Straight Point (AI Only) When DXF is imported from AI (Adobe illustrator), the curve information does not come in properly, which may distort part of the pattern. In this case, it can be solved by converting all the curved points of the pattern to straight points. Optimize All Curve Points Easily modify the curve by optimizing the number of curve points added on the line segment. Export Pattern Bounding Box (Single Bounding Box/ Separate Pattern Bounding Box) By exporting the pattern with the bounding box, conveniently edit the image when working in photoshop, illustration, etc. Export Selected Patterns (ver 6.1) Only the selected pattern is exported not the entire pattern.
